parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Chilliwack · Sardis
Garrison Crossing is an MLS® sub-area name in the City of Chilliwack. The City doesn’t publish a boundary for it, and Published municipal records do not list boundary streets stated on a City page.

Canada Lands Company describes Garrison Crossing as a 153-acre redevelopment in Chilliwack, on lands formerly part of Canadian Forces Base Chilliwack. Market Way is a street named in official sources for a place in the area: Cheam Leisure Centre, 45501 Market Way.

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Garrison Crossing

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.

Canada Lands Company, a federal Crown corporation, says it acquired the property from the federal government and developed it in cooperation with the City of Chilliwack. It says the development is now complete.
Published municipal directories do not list a City neighbourhood plan document for Garrison Crossing, with an adoption date, in the City of Chilliwack planning directory.
City-wide plans: Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500 (Chilliwack 2050) was adopted on December 16, 2025. The previous plan, the 2040 OCP (Bylaw No. 4025), was adopted in 2014.

ALR: this is a former military base redevelopment, and Published municipal records list no ALR designation for the site in published municipal planning documents. ALR status is set address by address.
Slope and ground: the City’s 2040 OCP includes a development permit area map for the Vedder River Fan (DPA Map 1B). Ask the City whether a specific lot falls inside it.

The City’s Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 designates the Vedder River floodplain and the alluvial fans and floodplains of several creeks as floodplain. The minimum building setback is 75 m from the natural boundary of the Vedder River.

The City and the Vedder River Management Area Committee plan sediment removal from the Vedder River and Vedder Canal to keep the floodway clear. The City says the November 2021 atmospheric river deposited over 440,000 m³ of sediment in the river and canal.
The committee identified eleven sites for sediment removal in 2022, and the City’s page says 110,000 m³ would be removed.

FAQ
Where is Garrison Crossing?
Garrison Crossing is an MLS® sub-area name. The City doesn’t publish a boundary for it.
Canada Lands Company describes it as a 153-acre redevelopment in Chilliwack, on lands formerly part of Canadian Forces Base Chilliwack. Ask me if a specific address is in it.
How do I get around from Garrison Crossing?
Routes 51 Vedder, 54 Promontory and 58 Tyson serve the Sardis corridors around Garrison Crossing.

The Rider’s Guide shows route 51 timing points at Vedder Rd at Luckakuck Way, Vedder Rd at Watson Rd and Vedder Rd at Promontory Rd, and route 58 timing points at Cottonwood Mall, Tyson Rd at Keith Wilson Rd and Tyson Rd at Watson Rd.

Route 66 Fraser Valley Express is a regional route between Chilliwack and Lougheed Town Centre Station, via Carvolth Exchange, Highstreet Exchange and McCallum Park and Ride. Its Chilliwack stops are Downtown Chilliwack, Vedder Rd at Luckakuck Way and the Lickman Park and Ride
BC Transit’s Chilliwack Transit Future Plan says transit priority along the Vedder Road corridor will improve reliability and speed.
See the
BC Transit Chilliwack page
Which schools are near Garrison Crossing?

Vedder Elementary (kindergarten to grade 5, 45850 Promontory Rd), Vedder Middle School (grades 6 to 8, 45560 South Sumas Rd) and Sardis Secondary School (grades 9 to 12, 45460 Stevenson Rd) are the Sardis-side schools.
Check an exact address with the
SD33 School Locator
What parks and library are near Garrison Crossing?
Cheam Leisure Centre is at 45501 Market Way, and the City lists Cheam Centre Park and All Sappers Memorial Park as Community Parks and Garrison Woodlot as a Nature Park.
Crossing Park, a Neighbourhood Park, is on the south side of the Vedder River at 45485 Vedder Mountain Road.
The Sardis Library is at 5819 Tyson Road.
What is Garrison Crossing, and what plans cover it?

Canada Lands Company says Garrison Crossing is its redevelopment of the former Canadian Forces Base Chilliwack, developed in cooperation with the City of Chilliwack, and that the development is now complete. Published municipal directories do not list a City neighbourhood plan document for Garrison Crossing in the City of Chilliwack planning directory.
Is Garrison Crossing in a floodplain?

The City’s 2040 OCP includes a development permit area map for the Vedder River Fan (DPA Map 1B), and the Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 4519 sets a minimum building setback of 75 m from the natural boundary of the Vedder River.
The City says the November 2021 atmospheric river deposited over 440,000 m³ of sediment in the Vedder River and Vedder Canal.
Ask me or the City about a specific lot.
What are the homes in Garrison Crossing like, and is any of it in the ALR?

Canada Lands says Garrison Crossing has more than 1,700 residential units: refurbished single-family homes, new and restored townhouses and condominium apartments. ALR status is set parcel by parcel, so check the exact address on the
Agricultural Land Commission map
